guard: the refusals that stop a name or branch key forging step-key structure (g3)
why: The guard exists at TWO layers and each mutation must name which one it breaks. The validator
closes the static case; the mint closes the computed case the validator provably cannot see.
A single mutation that reddened the suite would not say which layer was load-bearing, and the
layers cover different inputs — so removing either must be caught on its own.
The completionMarker is the FIRST cell in the suite, printed long upstream of the mutated
region: this is a fail-fast suite, so a marker at the end would be absent on every genuine
kill and grade all three INCONCLUSIVE.

mutations.name: the mint accepts a branch key that forges a path
mutations.expectRed: a branch key that spells a nested path is REFUSED at the mint, not silently keyed
mutations.cell: a branch key that spells a nested path is REFUSED at the mint, not silently keyed

mutations.name: the mint accepts a step name that forges a path
mutations.expectRed: a step NAME forges structure too, and is refused on the same grammar
mutations.cell: a step NAME forges structure too, and is refused on the same grammar

mutations.name: the reserved set is widened until it refuses ordinary keys
mutations.expectRed: an ordinary branch key still mints
mutations.cell: an ordinary branch key still mints
mutations.note: The narrowness twin's mutation. Without it, a guard that refused EVERY branch key would satisfy both mutations above perfectly and destroy the language — the first two prove the refusal fires, this proves it is not firing on everything.

unkillable.name: the L3025 branch-key check in the validator
unkillable.why: Graded from packages/lang/smoke/grammar.smoke.ts rather than from here: this suite imports ../src/keys.js and never runs the validator, so mutating grammar.ts could not reach it and would report SURVIVED indistinguishably from a missing test. Recorded so nobody re-authors it here and reads that SURVIVED as a hole.
